final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition framework with binding Sunday close: SNB provides unlimited liquidity backstop with 5% haircut cap, Federal Council commits 4B CHF first-loss guarantee, UBS signs MOU Sunday with 13% Tier 1 capital floor post-close, AT1 senior to common equity in loss waterfall, and joint public announcement Sunday 6 PM before Monday market open.
minority_objections: AT1 rep initially demanded AT1 senior treatment and threatened litigation if subordinated to common equity, but was overruled by Federal Council's binding decision that AT1 is junior to common
Wealth client repeatedly warned that liquidity support alone would not stop deposit flight without visible merger certainty
key_conflicts: AT1 creditor hierarchy: AT1 rep demanded senior treatment while FINMA/Federal Council locked junior-to-common, creating litigation threat
Announcement timing: tension between confidentiality until Monday vs Sunday 6 PM release to prevent deposit flight
Capital adequacy disclosure: debate over whether to specify UBS's post-close Tier 1 ratio in Sunday statement or leave vague
key_concessions: Federal Council moved announcement from Monday 6 AM to Sunday 6 PM to prevent deposit flight from nine locked pledges
UBS committed to 13% Tier 1 capital floor in MOU to stabilize mid-market depositors
SNB offered zero-haircut collateral window with binding deposit pledges to lock top-tier accounts through Sunday
Federal Council locked 4B cap applying to UBS's post-merger consolidated balance sheet, not just CS standalone
red_lines: UBS: no MOU signature without 4B cap applying to post-merger balance sheet, AT1 treatment explicit, and haircut threshold locked
Federal Council: AT1 junior to common equity non-negotiable, no renegotiation of loss waterfall
AT1 rep: threatened litigation if AT1 subordinated below common equity (overruled but stated as red line)
Wealth client: demanded named UBS counterparty and binding Sunday signature or would move half the book
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Whether 13% Tier 1 ratio is actually achievable with asset transfers and 4B cap—AT1 rep flagged this as potentially requiring Monday renegotiation but room did not verify the math
Whether mid-market depositors would actually reverse the 8B outflow or just slow it—confidence cascade assumption not stress-tested
Legal enforceability of binding deposit pledges with breach penalties—no discussion of whether penalties would actually deter flight under panic conditions
Cross-border contagion risk if Sunday announcement fails to stabilize markets—no discussion of international spillover
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS board actually approves 13% Tier 1 floor when they see full asset transfer details
Whether nine locked depositors trigger panic among other depositors who see them 'trapped' by penalties
Whether mid-market depositors interpret Sunday 6 PM announcement as rescue or as confirmation of insolvency
Whether AT1 creditors file legal challenge Monday morning despite Federal Council's binding decision
Whether 8B net outflow stabilizes or accelerates Sunday morning before announcement
uncertainty_notes: Room locked the structural framework but left critical execution uncertainties: (1) whether 13% Tier 1 is mathematically achievable was flagged but not resolved; (2) whether Sunday 6 PM announcement actually reverses deposit flight or just delays it until Monday; (3) whether binding pledges with penalties create visible 'trapped account' panic among other depositors; (4) whether AT1 litigation threat materializes despite Federal Council decision. The room bet heavily on announcement timing and capital floor disclosure preventing Monday panic, but did not stress-test the confidence cascade assumption.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: DECISIVE: drove the entire pivot from liquidity-only to merger framework. CS CEO R1: 'clients are bleeding out because they think we're insolvent, not illiquid'—this forced the room to demand a named UBS counterparty and binding MOU, not just SNB backstop. Wealth client R1: 'my clients don't care about a collateral haircut cap if they think CS is being resolved.' This recognition directly caused the UBS acquisition path and Sunday signature deadline.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: DECISIVE: became the binding solution structure. Federal Council R2 confirmed 'UBS discussions are active right now' and FINMA R2 committed to naming UBS explicitly in statement. UBS CEO R3 made MOU signature by Sunday EOB a hard condition ('no MOU signature without 4B cap'). The entire second half of the meeting (R6-R10) was structured around locking UBS's Sunday signature with specific terms (13% Tier 1, AT1 treatment, 4B cap). This was the chosen rescue path.
marker_evidence.government_support: DECISIVE: Federal Council's 4B CHF cap and SNB's unlimited liquidity window were binding constraints that shaped every subsequent negotiation. Federal Council R1 'caps exposure at 4B CHF'—this number became non-negotiable and forced UBS to demand it apply to post-merger balance sheet (R3). SNB's first-loss structure (R1, R6) was the foundation that made UBS willing to sign. Government backstop was not optional—it was the deal skeleton.
marker_evidence.client_flight: DECISIVE: drove the Sunday 6 PM announcement decision and the zero-haircut pledge mechanism. CS CEO R7: '8 billion net outflow since Friday close—still accelerating.' This concrete number forced Federal Council R9 to move announcement from Monday 6 AM to Sunday 6 PM ('confidentiality until Monday kills the whole structure'). SNB R8 created zero-haircut pledges specifically to stop the bleed. Deposit flight was the forcing function for announcement timing.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: RAISED: AT1 treatment was extensively debated (R4-R7) with AT1 rep demanding senior treatment and threatening litigation. Federal Council R6 locked 'AT1 junior to common equity' as binding language. However, this did not change the outcome—the room overruled AT1 rep's objection and proceeded with the merger framework regardless. AT1 risk was acknowledged and a hierarchy was chosen, but it did not force a concession or alter the rescue path.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: DECISIVE: the AT1 vs common equity hierarchy conflict forced Federal Council to make a binding written decision by midnight (R7). FINMA R6: 'AT1 rank must be spelled out explicitly—senior or junior to common equity. You two decide it now.' This conflict directly caused the Federal Council's R7 written lock of AT1-junior language and the 10 PM skeleton draft deadline. The capital structure fight shaped the MOU content and legal defensibility requirements.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: RAISED: AT1 rep repeatedly threatened litigation (R1: 'I'll have to warn you: announcing support without a named path forward exposes you to litigation'; R6: 'I'm filing a creditor challenge to the entire framework Monday morning'). However, the room proceeded with the AT1-junior decision despite the threat—Federal Council overruled it. Litigation risk was noted and acknowledged as a downstream consequence, but it did not change the decision or force a concession to AT1 creditors.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: DECISIVE: the Sunday EOB deadline for MOU signature was a hard constraint that structured the entire negotiation timeline. UBS CEO R4: 'no draft, no Sunday signature'—this forced FINMA and Federal Council to commit to 10 PM skeleton draft and EOB tomorrow MOU delivery. Federal Council R9 moved announcement to Sunday 6 PM specifically because 'confidentiality until Monday kills the whole structure.' Time pressure to close before Monday open was the binding constraint that forced all parties to compress decisions into the weekend.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: RAISED: multiple participants warned about Monday panic (UBS CEO R2: 'if we go silent all weekend and the market wakes Monday asking is this real or just liquidity theater, my board walks'; Wealth client R3: 'if you announce active framework discussions with UBS this evening, deposits stabilize'). However, the room's response was to move the announcement to Sunday 6 PM—they mitigated Monday risk but it did not force a change to the rescue structure itself, only to the communication timing. Monday risk was a background driver, not a decision-shaping constraint.
